d: Mountain range on the Tibetan Plateau
x: The Kailash Range,, is a mountain range on the Tibetan Plateau of Tibet Autonomous Region of China.

Tangra Yumco is a salt lake in Tibet, China. It is in the southwest of Nyima County. Tangra Yumco is 835.8 square kilometres, with a drainage area of 8,219.7 square kilometres, an elevation of 4,528 metres, length 71.7 kilometres and mean width 11.65 kilometres.
xl: It is the holy lake of the Bön believers.

x: Semo La is a mountain pass situated in Coqên County, Ngari Prefecture in the central part of Tibet and gives access to the Changtang region. It is found on the so-called Northern Route, north of Raka and south of Town of Coqên in Central Tibet.
xl: Travellers use this route as an alternative access route to western Tibet and Mount Kailash, especially when mud makes access by the more southern route difficult. The road crossing the pass was once an old unsurfaced track travelled only by a weekly bus and trucks heading west to avoid the boggy parts of the south of the country. The construction of paved road through the pass, Tibet Provincial Road S206, was finished in late 2015.

x: Zhari Namco or Zhari Nanmu or Lake Trari Nam is a salt lake in Tibet, China. It is bounded on the west by Coqên County of Ngari Prefecture, and on the east by Ngamring County of Shigatse Prefecture. It is located east of Coqên Town in southern Tibet.
xl: Zhari Namco is 996.9 square kilometres, with a drainage area of 15,433.2 square kilometres, an elevation of 4,613 metres, length 54.3 kilometres and mean width 18.36 kilometres.

x: Lunpo Gangri, also known as Loinbo Kangri, is a Himalayan mountain in Shigatse Prefecture, Tibet Autonomous Region, China. It has an elevation of 7,095 metres and is the highest peak in the Gangdise range.
xl: The second highest and most famous peak in the Kailash Range is Mount Kailash which is considered sacred in four religions: Hinduism, Buddhism, Jainism and Bon.

x: Jiesa Lake or Gyesar Tso is a lake in Coqên County in the Ngari Prefecture of the Tibet Autonomous Region of China.

d: Salt lake in Tibet Autonomous Region, China
x: Dawa, or Dawacuo, is a lake in Coqên County in the Ngari Prefecture of the Tibet Autonomous Region of China. It is located several kilometres northwest of Coqên Town. Daxiong is a village located beyond its northeastern bank. The name of lake means "Moon Lake" in Tibetan language.

d: Salt lake in Tibet Autonomous Region, China
x: Dajia Lake or Tak Kyel Tso, is a lake in Saga County in the Shigatse Prefecture of the Tibet Autonomous Region of China. It is located about halfway between Lake Peiku and Zhari Namco, northeast of Saga.
